claims.claim: Cipher's structural asset is access to large energized sites and interconnection, which can bridge electricity supply to AI/HPC compute demand; the economic bottleneck shifts from bitcoin-mining hardware toward grid access, construction delivery, cooling and tenant-ready infrastructure.

Long-term HPC leases can reduce bitcoin-price dependence, but rent begins only as phases are delivered, so construction and interconnection remain causal prerequisites rather than completed value capture.

causalEdges: AI compute demand -> demand for energized data-center capacity
construction completion -> lease commencement -> recurring rent

risks.risk: Interconnection and construction are successor bottlenecks after site/power acquisition.

unknowns.unknown: Stabilized tenant-level returns after full campus delivery remain unobserved.

claims.claim: Cipher's transition is heavily financed: total consolidated indebtedness was approximately $6.016 billion at June 30, 2026, while major HPC leases had not commenced and no lease revenue had yet been recognized.

The core risk is timing mismatch rather than evidence of thesis failure: debt and construction obligations exist before phased lease revenue, creating sensitivity to delays, cost overruns and tenant remedies.

causalEdges: construction delay -> delayed rent -> weaker debt coverage
bitcoin exposure during transition -> earnings volatility

risks.risk: Approximately $6.0B of indebtedness materially raises execution sensitivity during the HPC buildout.
Lease remedies and rent credits can reduce economics if delivery milestones are missed.

unknowns.unknown: Post-delivery cash yields and debt-service coverage for the new HPC campuses are not yet observable.
